Subject: Tokenization latency spike — urgent clarity requested

Hi Dylan,

We saw a large latency spike in tokenization calls to your hosted endpoint between 08:42–08:56 PDT this morning. P95 jumped from ~120ms to >3.2s, and several customer flows timed out. Our engineers flagged the window and collected traces — forwarding a short summary below.

Impact: ~12% transaction failures for our nightly batch run, some user-facing checkout timeouts.

Can you confirm what triggered the spike, what mitigation is in place, and when we can expect a detailed timeline + action plan? Our compliance team also asked for any logs/traces we can share for their audit.

Key traces attached in our system; happy to upload to a shared Drive if helpful. We need this consolidated by EOD tomorrow for our internal incident review.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Ops Lead — BlueHarbor Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tokenization latency spike — urgent clarity requested

Dylan / Hannah — quick internal sync so we have aligned customer messaging.

Summary of our current working hypothesis (do not share externally yet):
1) On 06/15 08:40 PDT we rolled a change that tightened batch aggregation thresholds for the tokenization stage to improve throughput for large payloads.
2) Under a specific short-sequence traffic pattern (seen in BlueHarbor traces) that included sporadic long-latency CPU-bound tokenization calls, the new thresholds inadvertently delayed batch flushes, causing a backlog and head-of-line effect across the tokenization workers.
3) The backlog increased queueing latency and amplified tail latency for unrelated short requests.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:15 PDT:
- Reverted batching threshold change (hotfix rollback).
- Enabled request-level preemption on the tokenization queue to prevent long-running tokenization from blocking short sequences.

Next steps (Marissa lead):
- Produce a customer-facing RCA with timeline and action items (deliverable: postmortem-debrief.pdf). Target: EOD 06/16.
- Collect and sanitize runtime traces and include them as an artifact.
- Propose permanent fixes: (a) enhanced batching policy with workload-aware thresholds, (b) per-request CPU budget and metrics, (c) a regression test covering the short-sequence heavy-tail pattern.

Hannah — confirm whether kernel trace shows any hardware-level anomaly or if this is purely scheduling/batching.

-Marissa
Senior CS Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <ops@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Tokenization latency spike — post-incident debrief and verification plan

Hi Elena / Tom — thank you again for the traces and patience while we completed the analysis. Attached is our post-incident package (postmortem-debrief.pdf) and supporting traces. Below is a concise customer-facing summary; the attached PDF contains the full timeline, all data artifacts, and verification steps your team can run.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-06-15 08:42–08:56 PDT.
- Root cause: a batching-aggregation threshold change rolled 08:40 PDT interacted with an uncommon short-sequence traffic pattern that included sporadic long-running tokenization CPU work. The change increased time-to-flush for tokenization batches, producing head-of-line blocking and amplified tail latency.
- Impact: increased P95/P99 tokenization latency, causing ~12% failed transactions for BlueHarbor's nightly batch and elevated user-facing checkout timeouts.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:40 PDT: deploy of batching threshold change.
- 08:42–08:56 PDT: observed latency spike; BlueHarbor alerts.
- 09:02 PDT: BlueHarbor initial contact to Redwood.
- 10:15 PDT: rollback of batching threshold; enabled preemption on tokenization queue.
- 10:20–11:00 PDT: metrics returned to baseline.

Action items (owner + ETA):
1) Permanent batching policy update — Marissa / Platform team — ETA 2027-07-02. Includes workload-aware thresholds and automated validation.
2) Per-request CPU budget and preemption guardrails — Hannah / Runtime — ETA 2027-06-28.
3) Regression test for short-sequence heavy-tail pattern — QA/Runtime — ETA 2027-06-25.
4) Post-deploy canary and telemetry alert for batch-aggregation anomalies — Observability — ETA 2027-06-24.

Artifacts and verification steps included in attachments:
- postmortem-debrief.pdf (full timeline, sanitized traces, root cause analysis)
- diag-tokenization-traces.zip (sample traces from affected window)
- proposed-mitigation-steps.md (detailed config changes and test plan)

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute verification call next week to walk through the artifacts and confirm your compliance/audit requirements are satisfied. Suggested slots: Tue 06/22 09:00–11:00 PDT or Wed 06/23 13:00–15:00 PDT. Please let us know what works.

Again, sincere apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as a priority program to prevent recurrence and will share incremental progress on the action items.

Best regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-debrief.pdf, diag-tokenization-traces.zip, proposed-mitigation-steps.md
